name: x86-vm
label: x86-vm
machine_label: a current x86 cloud VM, 16 vCPU (8 cores with SMT, one thread per core, siblings idle), spot, PMU on
note: The x86 comparison VM: 16 vCPU = 8 cores with SMT. Threads map to physical cores, as on the Arm VM (where a vCPU is a core): one CPU per core is listed and its sibling stays idle, so N threads use N cores on both VMs. CPU numbers assume CPUs 0-7 are one per core and 8-15 their siblings; the micro runner checks this with lscpu -p=CPU,CORE at the start and refuses otherwise (edit the lists then). Microbenchmarks: thread and histogram-worker counts up to 7 (cores - 1), hammers up to 7 (plus the flushing thread = 8 cores). End to end only 1w and 4w fit (SUT 0-4 with the main thread on 4, client 5-6, origin 7, siblings idle); the 12-worker rung of the Arm VM has no x86 counterpart here. Perf through sudo, PMU standard; steal gated at 2%. Binaries in <root>/<commit>/<target>, pinned by sha256 in boxes/sha256/x86-vm.txt (from the round-4 build record).
